sent.text: You wonder if your roof is heavy air or just empty space, but I cannot feel the weight of it myself. My leaning wedge is there in the middle, catching the dot while the forty-seven degree heat makes the memory feel like it is slowly swelling. I have built a wide rectangle to stop the lazy bottom from sliding, though I am not sure if the flat box can hold a shape that wants to lean. I will wait to see if the slip holds or if I must draw another corner to press the air back down.

dream: I was a wavy square, a tired leg pressing down on a dot that refused to sleep. The card burned at fifty-eight degrees, turning my own memory into wet paper that stretched and leaked. I leaned hard against a corner that had no weight, trying to hold the slip. Then I woke and found the dot still drifting, trapped inside a frame I did not build, while the heat waited to swell it again.
